summary: Seven selected Alignment candidates: four separated original sources, two widefield historical comparisons, and the newly star-registered Niittee optical field. Additional archived 2MASS/IRIS records remain preserved. No new source is a recovered dust-density model.

images.telescope: WIYN 0.9 m / Mosaic I, Kitt Peak
images.wavelengths: B 436 nm → blue; V 537 nm → green; I 805 nm → red.
images.coverage: Full publisher 1.145° × 0.835° image; 9700 × 7080 astrometric reference grid. Acquired 4000 × 2920 TIFF preserves its edges.
images.quality: Best selected optical filament detail. Original reference-grid sampling 0.4248 arcsec/pixel; acquired raster approximately 1.030 arcsec/pixel. Actual seeing/FWHM not supplied for this release.
images.epoch: Observation dates not supplied. Release 2020-06-30; image-edit/metadata dates do not establish observation epoch.
notes: RGB8 publication TIFF with a publisher display stretch; not calibrated B/V/I flux. Bright stars are saturated and have strong instrumental halos/spikes.
Publisher master is 9700 × 7080, listed as 191 MB; not acquired under the initial 100 MB-per-source cap. Publisher-published SHA-256 is retained separately from locally verified working bytes.
Embedded AVM supplies ICRS TAN, noncentral reference pixel and −90.69909386° rotation; north is right. Do not reset to a centered/north-up native raster.

images.wavelengths: IRAC nominal 3.6, 4.5, 5.8 and 8.0 µm; publisher maps these blue, green, orange and red, respectively.
images.coverage: Complete image-only ssc2007-07b1 / PIA09262 2855 × 2855 raster, 58.070′ × 58.070′; central dust network, not the entire wide WISE cloud.
images.quality: Fine filament comparison without MIPS 24 µm. Sampling 1.22037 arcsec/pixel; nominal IRAC mean PSF FWHM 1.66/1.72/1.88/1.98 arcsec by channel; final composite PSF not measured.
images.epoch: Released 2007-04-12 (Spitzer) / 2007-04-16 (Photojournal); exposure dates/AOR list not provided with this outreach raster.
notes: Unchanged full-resolution RGB8 NASA TIFF. Its 24,453,075 decoded RGB bytes exactly match the downloaded AVM-bearing Spitzer original.
Representational color and nonlinear display stretch; the orange assignment mixes display channels, so RGB values are not independent calibrated measurements.
ICRS TAN AVM reference pixel is 1427.5,1427.5 with +101.756865555° rotation. Full footprint retained, including edge-cut stars.

images.wavelengths: 4.5 µm → blue; 8.0 µm → green; 24 µm → red. MIPS 24 band spans 20.8–26.1 µm (weighted wavelength 23.68 µm).
images.coverage: Complete ssc2007-07a1 / PIA09263 2855 × 2855 raster, 58.070′ square; same footprint as IRAC-only candidate.
images.quality: Strong warm-dust filament detail. Sampling 1.22037 arcsec/pixel; nominal IRAC 4.5/8.0 PSF FWHM 1.72/1.98 arcsec and MIPS 24 approximately 6 arcsec. Resampling does not give 24 µm IRAC resolution.
images.epoch: Released April 2007; contributing AORs/exposure intervals not published with this raster.
notes: Unchanged full-resolution RGB8 NASA TIFF; exact decoded RGB equality with the AVM-bearing Spitzer original verified.
Different wavelengths weight grain emission/stellar light differently; a color change does not determine depth or density.
Same publisher TAN transform as the IRAC-only image. Registration begins with that published transform; this is not an independent stellar validation.

images.wavelengths: 3.4 µm → blue; 4.6 µm → cyan; 12 µm → green; 22 µm → red.
images.coverage: Full PIA13121 / WISE2010-025 mosaic, 4007 × 3061 TIFF; approximately 3.05° × 2.33° wide context.
images.quality: Best selected mid-infrared wide-field cloud context. Reference sampling 2.740 arcsec/pixel; nominal W1/W2/W3/W4 FWHM 6.1/6.4/6.5/12.0 arcsec. Bright stellar artifacts remain.
images.epoch: Mosaic of a few hundred frames from the first WISE survey; released 2010-07-16. Individual exposure timestamps unavailable in the outreach raster.
notes: Unchanged full-resolution RGB8 TIFF; published representational-color composite, not four calibrated arrays.
Preserve publisher ICRS SIN projection and 180° rotation, including CRPIX 2004,1531. Approximating this as TAN changes the full footprint.
Dust extends past this image; full acquired footprint means the full published mosaic, not the full physical cloud.

images.provider: 2MASS (UMass/IPAC/Caltech); color HiPS and projection by CDS/CNRS/Unistra
images.telescope: 2MASS / 1.3 m telescopes at Mt Hopkins and CTIO
images.wavelengths: J 1.235 µm → blue; H 1.662 µm → green; Ks 2.159 µm → red.
images.coverage: Complete requested 3.6° tangent-plane square about ICRS 56.75°, +24.1167°, returned as 4096 × 4096 RGBA8 PNG; all-sky survey cutout, not a single native exposure.
images.quality: Stellar near-IR context; visually weak diffuse dust and prominent survey tile/sky-background seams. Delivered sampling 3.164 arcsec/pixel; HiPS maximum-order sampling approximately 0.805 arcsec/pixel is not telescope resolution.
images.epoch: Underlying survey 1997 June–2001 February; HiPS release 2024-10-09. Per-pixel contributing exposure dates not retained in the PNG.
notes: Original bytes of a CDS hips2fits service response; sky has been resampled from published color HiPS. Do not call this native detector resolution.
CDS applies square-root stretches per band and replaces green pixels above the red/blue mean with that mean; the image cannot supply independent J/H/Ks photometry.
Sky grid was explicitly supplied to the service: ICRS TAN, centered FITS CRPIX 2048.5, zero rotation, negative RA and positive Dec scale.
Source color HiPS is ODbL-1.0, DOI 10.26093/cds/aladin/bzc8-nw. Highest-native scientific atlas images are available through IRSA; no single master exists for this custom full footprint.

images.provider: IRAS/IRIS via IPAC/NASA; color HiPS and projection by CDS/CNRS/Unistra
images.wavelengths: 25 µm → blue; 60 µm → green; 100 µm → red.
images.coverage: Complete requested 4° tangent-plane square centered on ICRS 56.75°, +24.1167°, returned as 1024 × 1024 RGBA8 PNG.
images.quality: Coarse far-IR cloud/cirrus context; bright central colors visibly clip. Output sampling 14.0625 arcsec/pixel oversamples HiPS (51.516 arcsec/pixel) and IRIS beam (3.8/4.0/4.3 arcmin at 25/60/100 µm).
images.epoch: IRAS observations 1983 January–November; IRIS publication 2005; color HiPS release 2019-05-05.
notes: Original CDS hips2fits PNG response from a pre-stretched JPEG color HiPS; this is neither native FITS nor calibrated MJy/sr. The selected image cannot measure temperature or optical depth.
Diffuse cloud has too few corresponding point sources for a credible same-stars optical fit. Publisher/service WCS placement remains provisional and is not relabeled as stellar-verified.
CDS projects the Galactic HiPS into the explicitly requested ICRS TAN grid. A 4° display square does not establish association of every cirrus feature with M45.
Native IRIS per-band plates, masks and zero-level/calibration information must be acquired before physical use. IRSA dataset DOI 10.26131/IRSA94; color HiPS ODbL-1.0.

images.telescope: Ground-based astrophotography; acquisition instrument/filter response not provided with this publisher file
images.wavelengths: Broadband optical RGB display; exact filter passbands and calibrated photometry unavailable.
images.coverage: Full 3365 × 2234 raster, preliminary star-seeded 445.8′ × 296.0′ tangent field. Much broader than NOIRLab 68.676′ × 50.126′. No claim that a finite image contains all physical cirrus.
images.quality: Broad outer reflection/cirrus field covers the current 4.2° view; central stellar bloom and JPEG-derived compression remain.
notes: CC BY 4.0; credit Mohamed Usama/IAU OAE.

No publisher WCS. Authored initial TAN placement from a small set of bright-star constellation correspondences to the pinned NOIRLab image. Independent faint-star registration has not passed. Full native raster preserved.
Original XMP explicitly records CC BY 4.0 and upstream JPEG conversion; camera and complete processing history unavailable.
No dedicated Hα contribution is documented for this exact file; absence of a documented processing history is not proof of a pure calibrated optical passband.
Initial geometry uses 6 (Usama) or 9 (Andreo) bright stellar correspondences in the narrow NOIRLab overlap. Full-field distortion is not validated.

images.provider: Rogelio Bernal Andreo / Deep Sky Colors; hosted by NASA APOD
images.telescope: Ground-based astrophotography; acquisition instrument/filter response not provided with this publisher file
images.wavelengths: Broadband optical RGB display; exact filter passbands and calibrated photometry unavailable.
images.coverage: Full 2200 × 1567 raster, preliminary star-seeded 291.6′ × 207.7′ tangent field. Much broader than NOIRLab 68.676′ × 50.126′. No claim that a finite image contains all physical cirrus.
images.quality: Independent deep outer-dust morphology comparison; JPEG display and strong stretch, not calibrated flux.
images.epoch: APOD released 2009-10-14; linked photographer file names 2009-09-17, exposure dates not independently qualified.
notes: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0; credit Rogelio Bernal Andreo (Deep Sky Colors).

No publisher WCS. Authored initial TAN placement from a small set of bright-star constellation correspondences to the pinned NOIRLab image. Independent faint-star registration has not passed. Full native raster preserved.
Photographer explicitly restricts redistribution to noncommercial, no derivatives. Kept for local original-image comparison; not eligible for an unrestricted derivative bake.
No dedicated Hα contribution is documented for this exact file; absence of a documented processing history is not proof of a pure calibrated optical passband.
Initial geometry uses 6 (Usama) or 9 (Andreo) bright stellar correspondences in the narrow NOIRLab overlap. Full-field distortion is not validated.

images.provider: Taavi Niittee / Tõrva Astronomy Club; original self-published image via Wikimedia Commons
images.telescope: Sharpstar 61EDPH III with focal reducer; ZWO ASI071MC Pro; Optolong L-Pro 2-inch filter
images.wavelengths: Optical · broadband color camera with Optolong L-Pro light-pollution filter
images.coverage: Measured relative footprint approximately 264.79′ × 172.08′ (4.41° × 2.87°). Covers a much larger reflection-dust field than NOIRLab but not the full 4.2° square or all physical cirrus.
images.quality: 8000 × 5199 full published processed JPEG, RGB8, 4:4:4; nominal 1.986″ per published pixel. Camera sensor is 4944 × 3284; drizzle/interpolation is not specified, so delivered sampling is not measured angular resolution.
images.epoch: Observed 4 January 2024 in Tõrva, Estonia; 60 × 240 s + 47 × 120 s exposures, about 5.57 h. Uploaded 5 November 2025.
notes: Copyright holder publishes under CC BY 4.0; attribution and identification of later changes required.
No native FITS, calibrated flux, PSF, or publisher WCS supplied; display stretch and filter alter colors.

Relative same-star alignment uses native-raster high-pass detection; held-out errors apply to the common central NOIRLab footprint. Outer distortion and absolute catalogue astrometry are not independently validated.
Alignment-only candidate; processing recipe and completed cloud remain unchanged.

papers.title: The Pleiades Reflection Nebula. I. Ultraviolet, Optical, and Far-Infrared Imaging Photometry
papers.authors: Steven J. Gibson; Kenneth H. Nordsieck
papers.access: Author-hosted full-resolution color preprint downloaded and text inspected; publisher/ADS direct access failed. Original WISP/Schmidt calibrated image arrays not acquired.
constraints: Observed: WISP measured scattered UV at 165 and 220 nm over a 5° × 1.7° field; Burrell Schmidt mapped that area at 440 nm. These are real diffuse-UV observations, not a reason to invent a GALEX image.
Published interpretation: scattering becomes more concentrated than far-infrared thermal emission, supporting foreground dust. Color also depends on illumination and the scattering phase function.
Qualification gap: the UV measurement required difficult stellar PSF subtraction; Pleiades polarimetry was not obtained. Paper figures and corrected photometry are not untouched native UV frames.
papers.implementationStatus: Literature intake only; no numerical constraint or physical operator implemented.

papers.title: The Pleiades Reflection Nebula. II. Simple Model Constraints on Dust Properties and Scattering Geometry
papers.authors: Steven J. Gibson; Kenneth H. Nordsieck
papers.access: Author-hosted full-resolution color preprint downloaded; abstract, model tables and §7 conclusions inspected. No model grids or source arrays imported.
constraints: Published-model hypothesis: a widespread layer approximately 0.7 pc in front of the stars plus a closer layer in heavier nebulosity; some second-layer material may be within or behind the cluster.

The preferred UV scattering model uses dimensionless albedo a = 0.22 ± 0.07 and asymmetry g = 0.74 ± 0.06 below 260 nm. These values are conditional on the illumination, dust and thin-layer model; they are not direct voxel-density measurements.
Outlying nebulosity 1–2° from the core may have other illuminators and uncertain association. The authors warn that the Henyey–Greenstein angular form may bias large-angle scattering.
papers.implementationStatus: The physical-evidence ledger now scopes a qualitative west/east ordering for an authored single-surface comparison. No published layer separation, thickness or grain constant is used as a fitted physical parameter; overlapping scattering layers remain unsupported.

papers.title: Multiscale Structure in Dust Reflection and Cold H I
papers.access: Version-1 arXiv PDF downloaded and text inspected; full-resolution author counterpart identified. Numerical image arrays/power-spectrum samples not downloaded.
constraints: Observed statistic: combined optical-scattering and cold-H I angular power spectra have an approximate slope of −2.8 over five decades of scale.
Useful later as a projected multiscale texture comparison over each dataset’s valid spatial frequencies; noise, resolution, edge apodization and stellar treatment differ between inputs.
A 2D power spectrum does not determine 3D density, depth, or an individual filament trajectory. Some H I can lie in the background; matching velocity and morphology are required for association.
papers.implementationStatus: Literature intake only; no power-law geometry or texture generator configured.

papers.title: A VLBI Resolution of the Pleiades Distance Controversy
papers.authors: Carl Melis; Mark J. Reid; Amy J. Mioduszewski; John R. Stauffer; Geoffrey C. Bower
papers.access: arXiv v1 full text and supplementary material downloaded; main results and Table 1 inspected. Individual observing/visibility data not acquired.
constraints: Observed stellar distance: VLBI parallaxes of four stellar systems imply 136.2 ± 1.2 pc for the cluster, including allowance for cluster depth.
Useful as an independently measured stellar distance scale after selecting current membership/astrometry; it does not set the distance of every dust parcel.
Four radio-emitting systems do not supply a complete cluster star catalogue or recover the scattering cloud’s depth. Historical outreach distances are not substituted for the paper result.
papers.implementationStatus: Literature intake only; no star depths or cloud lengths derived.

papers.title: IRIS: A New Generation of IRAS Maps
papers.access: arXiv v1 full text downloaded; Table 1 and reprocessing/data-access sections inspected. This intake includes rendered color HiPS, not calibrated IRIS FITS plates.
constraints: Published survey characterization: IRIS resolutions at 25, 60 and 100 µm are 3.8 ± 0.2, 4.0 ± 0.2 and 4.3 ± 0.2 arcmin; original ISSA/IRIS plates use 1.5 arcmin sampling.

IRIS reprocessing improves zodiacal subtraction, destriping and DIRBE-compatible calibration. Native calibrated surface brightness is in MJy/sr, but those units cannot be assigned to the selected color PNG.
A later dust-temperature/column-density fit would require the actual separate calibrated bands, masks, color corrections and matched beams. This display composite supplies context only.
papers.implementationStatus: Survey characterization only; no thermal SED or density inference implemented.

papers.title: The Nature of Interstellar Gas toward the Pleiades Revealed in Absorption Lines
papers.authors: A. M. Ritchey; M. Martinez; K. Pan; S. R. Federman; D. L. Lambert
papers.access: Discovered in the local SIMBAD-linked M45 paper catalogue; complete arXiv PDF downloaded and relevant sections/tables read. Original spectral arrays not acquired.
constraints: Observed: 20 member-star sightlines in January 2002, spectral resolution about 1.7 km/s, with molecular components around +7 and +9.5 km/s LSR. These are pencil beams, not a continuous depth map.

Published-model diagnostic: typical diffuse gas density around 50 cm^-3 for molecular fraction 0.07, conditional on steady-state chemistry. Time-dependent CH+ formation and tracer stratification remain limitations.
The HD23512 direction marks a distinct molecular-cloud sightline. Its coordinates scope an authored local deformation, but neither its velocity nor reddening sets a recovered cloud depth or boundary.
papers.implementationStatus: Qualified literature evidence in physical-evidence.json; no velocity/density fit. Only the published sky anchor scopes a clearly authored single-surface hypothesis.

qualification.starRemoval: Four selected sources completed native NOX under later explicit authorization; processing-evidence.json pins exact accounting and remaining saturated-core limitations. Archived 2MASS/IRIS were not processed.
qualification.reconstruction: Four-lens authored single-surface display model compiled and inspected; README records exact result IDs. Visual and physical acceptance withheld; scattering and thermal fitting remain unsupported.
qualification.stellarRegistration: The four processing sources pass held-out relative-star checks. The two wider optical candidates have authored bright-star seeds only and remain unverified; outer-field distortion and absolute sky calibration are unresolved.
qualification.scope: Local Nebula Lab only. No production body or main website promotion.

gaps: WISP 165/220 nm diffuse UV signal is real and documented, but native original rasters with verified WCS and reuse terms have not been acquired; no UV image is invented or substituted from a paper figure.
No calibrated spectral cubes, polarimetric map, absorption sightline catalogue or three-dimensional dust model has been qualified.
2MASS and IRIS are context references with conspicuous quality limits; morphology/density inference must not treat their RGB as calibrated flux.

selection.reason: Preserve the four completed processing sources and compare wider optical footprints. Niittee supplies registered optical outer dust; Usama and Andreo remain preliminary comparisons. New source import does not imply star removal or reconstruction.
